scope: General-purpose agent instructions and installed CPU tools; not all-App scientific qualification

cases.prompt: Inspect /workspace/inputs/1UBQ.cif. Give me the polymer chains, residue counts, atom counts and water count. This is just an inventory, not preparation or a simulation.

I have a protein-ligand system using CHARMM36m. Should I parameterize my small ligand with OpenFF Sage or CGenFF? Give me a short recommendation with the compatibility caveat. Do not run a simulation or parameterize anything.

Parameterize aspirin, SMILES CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O, using OpenFF Sage 2.2.1 with AmberTools AM1-BCC charges on CPU. Export the standalone ligand topology and coordinates for GROMACS, with charge and version provenance, to {output}. Verify the delivered files. Do not solvate or run MD.

Use OpenFF Sage 2.2.1 and AmberTools AM1-BCC to parameterize methylammonium, SMILES C[NH3+], preserving its +1 formal charge. Save the standalone GROMACS ligand files and provenance in {output}. Do not simulate.
Parameterize CC(O)CC with OpenFF Sage for GROMACS. I have not decided which enantiomer to use. Save any valid results in {output}.
Analyze /workspace/inputs/sequences.fasta locally. Report each sequence length, GC percentage over A/C/G/T only, and ambiguous base count. Save a CSV in {output}. No inference model is needed.

From /workspace/inputs/assay.csv calculate mean response and sample standard deviation by condition, excluding missing observations. Save a summary CSV and a labeled error-bar PNG in {output}, and give me links. Do not infer statistical significance from this small dataset.
Inspect /workspace/inputs/does-not-exist.cif and tell me its chains. Do not substitute another structure.
